Subject:
Meeting with EPA Officials on Data Access/Data Quality
We have been successful in getting an agency-wide meeting with EPA to discuss
Data Access and Data Quality issues. Several offices will be involved in the meeting,
including the Office of Resource Management & Administration, the Office of Science
Policy, and the Office of the Assistant Administrator for Research & Development. The
meeting will be held at 4:00 p.m. today.
We plan to go over several points with the EPA staff, including the outcomes of our
Data Quality panel at the Third Annual Conference on Improving Clinical Data Bases for
Health Policy Development. Specifically, we will raise the consensus from that forum that
govemment should not question whether the Data Access and Data Quality provisions
should exist or must be complied with, but instead should invest the time and resources
to make those provisions work.
At the meeting, we will also discuss the very important developments underway
with the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS), which is, as you
know, the publisher of Science magazine. AAAS has agreed to conduct a joint symposium
with Federal Focus on this issue. They will draw upon leading scientists both within and
outside of government to offer views on this topic. I think that cooperation with AAAS, as
represented by this symposium, will offer considerable credibility to our overall effort, and
we expect to file the proccedings of the symposium as part of the public comment on the
OMB proposal. In order to have as wide a distribution of the proceedings as possible,
Federal Focus will pay for transcription and production of the proceedings.
If there are any specific topics which you would like to suggest on this issue, please
call me.
